variants.headline: Foreign scrollwork sets the fashion in our streets
body: A cartwright has painted the foreign scrollwork on a farmer's wagon, and the farmer paid extra to have it. Foreign influence over us has crossed into Influential at {{percentage}} percent. The cartwright now keeps the pattern on a board by the door.

variants.headline: In this year the voice of {{rival}} grew strong
body: It is recorded that in this year {{rival}} reached the Influential mark among our people, and the count was set at {{percentage}} percent. In the guild hall, apprentices now learn a pattern from across the border before they learn the one their masters cut.

variants.headline: What the children are singing
body: {{rival}} has reached the Influential mark over us. At the market, a child sang a tune she'd picked up from a traveling player. Her father says she knows the whole thing, verse after verse. Councilors, where in this town can a singer of our own make enough to buy supper?

variants.headline: The teacher stops correcting the words
body: The teacher at the school off the tanners' lane has stopped correcting the words of the new song; the children bring it in finished. Foreign influence over us has reached {{percentage}} percent, the mark the clerks call Influential. A peddler at the gate sells the song on a folded sheet.

variants.headline: Our blue bolt sets the fashion across the border
body: A draper on the high street has doubled her order of the blue bolt that sells across the border. Our plays, our cloth and our songs now set the fashion in the streets abroad, and our pull there has passed into Influential at {{percentage}} percent.

variants.headline: Hear it! {{rival}} knows our jokes
body: Hear it, people! Our influence over {{rival}} has reached the Influential mark at {{percentage}} percent. Their players are telling our jokes, and their crowds are laughing in the right places. They know the jokes, neighbors!

variants.headline: Our books could go farther through {{rival}}
body: Our influence over {{rival}} has reached the Influential mark at {{percentage}} percent. If printers there can sell enough copies to pay for translations, our writers gain a way to reach readers beyond both countries. A bookseller across a second border might find it cheaper to order those editions than to commission new ones.

variants.headline: Full houses, and the applause is sincere
body: Letters from a rival capital relate that our plays now play to standing crowds there, and that the house is full again the moment the doors open. The official count agrees: our influence in that nation has crossed into Influential. "The applause," our correspondent writes, "is not given to be polite."

variants.headline: The tailor clears his window: our pull slips to {{level}}
body: A tailor on the cobbled lane has cleared the foreign patterns from his window and hung his own cut in their place. The rival's hold over us has fallen from {{previousLevel}} to {{level}}, to {{percentage}} percent, and the local cloth is moving again.

variants.headline: {{rival}} loses its grip on our tastes
body: The singing master at the guild school has taken the {{rival}} air off the spring program and put a local ballad in its place. The rival's hold over us has slipped from {{previousLevel}} to {{level}}. Half the hall already knew the chorus of the replacement.

variants.headline: The market remembers its own
body: The hold of {{rival}} over us has eased to {{level}}. In the market, a potter has put her mother's clay cups back on the stall. "I'll make another dozen if these go," she says. She looks to the people who stop at her stall to tell her what to make next. The big shops would do well to listen to them too.

variants.headline: In this year the foreign fashion faded
body: It is recorded that the influence of a foreign people over our nation fell in this year from {{previousLevel}} to {{level}}. The elders note that the young are singing the old songs again, learned from grandmothers. What was borrowed is slowly being returned.

variants.headline: Our cloth moves back as influence eases to {{level}}
body: At the export house, a warehouseman has moved our bolt cloth to the back shelf. Our influence over that rival people has fallen from {{previousLevel}} to {{level}}, to {{percentage}} percent.

variants.headline: Where our influence slipped in {{rival}}
body: Our influence over {{rival}} has slipped from {{previousLevel}} to {{level}}. A printer who once sent new plays abroad has a shelf of unsold copies, and the council ought to ask whether booksellers there stopped ordering them or simply found a cheaper way to print their own.

variants.headline: Our fashions carry less weight in {{rival}}
body: Letters from {{rival}} relate that our styles no longer set theirs as they did; a tailor of that capital, once famous for copying our cuts, has put away his patterns of ours. By the recorded count, our influence there has fallen from {{previousLevel}} to {{level}}.

variants.headline: They've stopped singing our songs
body: A trader back from the foreign port was asked if they still sing our songs there. He shrugged. "They know the words," he said. "They've stopped singing them." The count of our influence abroad has fallen to {{level}}.

variants.headline: Foreign influence over us turns {{trend}}
body: The influence a rival nation holds over our people has turned {{trend}}, after {{previousTrend}}. The count stands at {{percentage}} percent, graded {{level}}. At the print shop, the compositor has set the new count in larger type than the old, and the master let it stand.

variants.headline: Foreign influence has {{turnsToInfluential}} turns to Influential, a schoolmaster bets
body: A schoolmaster has ordered a second printing of the foreign songbook before the term ends, on the guess that demand will last. Foreign influence over us has turned {{trend}}, and by the count it has {{turnsToInfluential}} turns to reach Influential. If the guess is wrong, the extra copies will sit in his cupboard.

variants.headline: The cloth sellers knew before the scribes did
body: There is an argument at the cloth stalls this season, and the wives conduct it loudly: the foreign bolt or the local weave, which does the town want? The count has come in from the scribes, and the influence of {{rival}} over us has turned {{trend}}. The stalls will tell you they knew it first.

variants.headline: The influence ledger
body: Foreign influence over us: {{level}}
Count at last reckoning: {{percentage}} percent
Direction: {{trend}}, after {{previousTrend}}

variants.headline: Our influence abroad turns {{trend}}
body: Our influence over a rival people has turned {{trend}}, after {{previousTrend}}. The count stands at {{percentage}} percent, graded {{level}}. At the export house, the clerk has last season's order book open beside this one and runs a finger down both columns before he quotes a price.

variants.headline: Forecast: {{turnsToInfluential}} turns to Influential
body: Our influence abroad is {{trend}}. The forecast gives us {{turnsToInfluential}} turns to reach Influential. At the export house, the shipping agent has left the autumn order sheet half filled.

variants.headline: Our fashions rise again in {{rival}}
body: Letters from {{rival}} relate that our styles are once more in the ascendant there. A hostess of that capital is said to have apologized to her guests for serving a native wine. The recorded count agrees: our influence has turned Rising, at the {{level}} grade.

variants.headline: In this year our word carried less weight
body: It is recorded that our influence over {{rival}} turned from Rising to Falling in this year, and rests at the {{level}} grade. The chronicle notes that fewer of their young came to study at our schools. The scribes set the change down as it was measured.

variants.headline: Culture is a front line too
body: Our influence over a rival has turned {{trend}}, resting at the {{level}} grade. The officers at the border posts have a use for that number. In a village that knows our songs and buys our pots, a patrol can ask the way to the ford and get an answer. In one that knows neither, every stranger is watched from the doorway. A column that has to pass through the second kind of village loses a day before it ever sees the enemy.

variants.headline: {{city}} completes the {{wonder}} under an enemy flag
body: A shepherd on the border ridge can see the {{wonder}} finished above the walls of {{city}}. The work went up through the whole war, stone on stone, and the war did not stop it.

variants.headline: An enemy city completes a wonder near our border
body: The {{wonder}} is complete in an enemy city close to our own towns.

variants.headline: The {{wonder}} at {{city}} frees its masons for war
body: The {{wonder}} at {{city}} is finished, and the masons who raised it are looking for their next wages. A nation at war has work for hands like those. A yard that can set a course of stone that true can set a rampart just as well. Where the enemy sends them next, a wall will follow.

variants.headline: A fine hall under a hostile flag
body: Advice reaches this office that the {{wonder}} now stands finished in enemy {{city}}, and that the workmanship is very fine; our correspondent confesses he stood a long while before it. Whatever banner hangs above it, the masons deserve their fee. It is a melancholy thing that so fine a hall should rise under a hostile sky.

variants.headline: The herd boys came back talking of towers
body: The herd boys came down at dusk talking of towers across the line, taller than anything on our side. The enemy city of {{city}} has raised the {{wonder}}, and the boys argued all the way home about what it was for. The capital can call the war its own affair. When you can see the enemy's towers from the pasture, the war is yours too.

variants.headline: {{cityName}} completes the {{wonder}}
body: The {{wonder}} stands finished in {{cityName}}, a city of {{civilization}}. Word of the work arrived with the last stones set, and already our own travelers are asking the way there.

variants.headline: A wonder finished abroad
body: The {{wonder}} now stands complete in a foreign city. Word of the work reached us after the scaffolds came down, and already the travelers are changing their routes to take it in.

variants.headline: The {{wonder}} makes {{civilization}} hard to forget
body: The {{wonder}} is complete in {{civilization}}. A correspondent there says his editor keeps asking for another column on it. What our own planners should notice is how much space a single work can earn in papers that usually print that country's name only when its ministers make news.

variants.headline: They will walk you through every stone
body: They say the scaffolds came down at {{cityName}} this season, and the {{wonder}} stood in the open air for the first time. The travelers back from {{cityName}} talk of little else. Let one of them buy you a drink and you will hear about every stone twice.

variants.headline: The {{wonder}} at {{cityName}} is complete
body: Letters from {{cityName}} relate that the {{wonder}} now stands finished there, and that visitors of every nation are already on the road to see it; our own included, the innkeepers say. Whatever divides the courts, a work like this is a pleasure shared. May it long draw a crowd.

variants.headline: A name for the histories is born in {{civilization}}
body: {{person}} has been born in {{civilization}}. By evening the neighbors had filled the doorstep with small gifts, and a scribe had come to write the name in the margin of the year.

variants.headline: A name for the histories is born
body: {{person}} has come into the world, and no one yet agrees which court may claim them. Envoys from more than one have already called at the house, and the family has not decided whom to receive.

variants.headline: In this year a {{unit}} came to {{civilization}}
body: It is recorded for this year that {{civilization}} received the {{unit}} {{person}}, newly come into the world. The scribes have set the name down in the margin as well as the line, which is done for no ordinary name.

variants.headline: A room is cleared before the work is chosen
body: {{person}} is ours. A porter at the works has been told to clear a room and find a bed before the week is out, and nobody has told him what work the room is for. The council has not decided whether the work is art, state or war. The room will be furnished first.

variants.headline: Citizens! A rival has a name we lack
body: Citizens, mark it: {{civilization}} counts {{person}} among its own, and we do not. Their gates have a new name to carve over them, and ours have none. Say what you like about friendship; the ledger does not read speeches.

variants.headline: The death of {{person}}
body: The bells of {{civilization}} rang at noon for {{person}}, and the square filled before they stopped. The name was known far beyond that nation's borders, and the news is traveling as far now.

variants.headline: The world is one name poorer
body: {{person}} of {{civilization}} is dead. The name was spoken in many lands in life, and the work left behind is written where no fire reaches. In the shrines, a lamp has been lit beside the name, and the wardens mean to keep it burning through the season.

variants.headline: {{killer}} kills {{person}}
body: {{person}} of {{civilization}} has died at the hands of {{killer}}. The news reached the barracks before it reached the family, and the sergeant read it twice before he posted it. Nobody in the yard spoke.

variants.headline: They sat late at the fires tonight
body: They sat late at the fires tonight. {{person}}, one of our own, is gone, and nobody wanted to be the first to leave the light. The stories about {{person}} started before the fire burned low, and by tomorrow every hearth will have its favorite.

variants.headline: Somebody sent {{person}} to their death
body: {{person}} is dead at the hands of {{killer}}. Greatness does not walk onto a battlefield by accident; somebody gave the orders that put one of our finest within an enemy's reach, and that somebody has a name and a desk. We want the name. We want the orders read aloud in council.

variants.headline: {{person}}'s study is cleared and the door locked
body: In {{civilization}}, the study that {{person}} kept has been cleared and the books crated for the guild. The work is finished, the gift is spent, and the door is locked behind it.

variants.headline: Notice: {{person}} spent in the nation's service
body: Notice is given that {{person}} has been spent in the nation's service. The council turned the gift to a purpose of state with its usual foresight. The particulars are not for every eye, and the public's thanks are owed.

variants.headline: A talent spent is a bet on the present
body: Spending {{person}} converts a whole future into one immediate act, and {{civilization}} has placed that bet. The sums will show in time whether the trade was wise. The person was not consulted.

variants.headline: The autograph he missed
body: A boy in {{civilization}} saved the last page of his copybook for {{person}} to sign. Now that the work was done, his father told him he'd missed his chance. The boy wrote the name himself. "The first letter's got to be big," he told his little brother.

variants.headline: New works on the walls of {{city}}
body: The hanging crew in {{city}} has been up the ladders since dawn, moving one frame to make room for the next. The walls now hold {{added}} more works than they did, {{total}} in all.

variants.headline: Notice to lovers of the arts
body: {{city}} is richer by {{added}} great works, making {{total}} in all. The galleries keep their usual hours. Linger as long as you like; the guards have been told to expect it.

variants.headline: A neighboring gallery asks {{city}} for a winter loan
body: {{city}} has added {{added}} works to its collection, bringing it to {{total}}. The neighboring town gallery has offered to send its wagon, with freshly made crates, for a winter loan. A loan on those terms could let small towns show works they can't afford to buy.

variants.headline: The crates came up from the docks before dawn
body: The crates came up from the docks before dawn, and by evening {{added}} new works hung in the galleries of {{city}}. The first admirers had waited at the door since noon, and the guards gave up shooing them off when the queue reached the fountain.

variants.headline: Great works lost from the galleries of {{city}}
body: The galleries of {{city}} are {{lost}} great works lighter than at the last count; {{total}} remain. A gallery hand has measured the bare spaces twice and put the tape away without cutting a frame.

variants.headline: The walls of {{city}} are barer
body: The galleries of {{city}} held more at their height. {{lost}} great works are gone from the walls, and {{total}} remain. At closing, the attendant walks the rooms and counts the hooks that hold nothing.

variants.headline: Print the names of the missing works
body: The new count of great works in {{city}} is down by {{lost}}. If the works were sent away, let the council say where we can see them. If they are lost, let it print their names. A reader might know where a missing work went, if we can tell her which one it is.

variants.headline: The nail is still in the wall
body: The old keeper says the nail is still in the wall, right where the painting hung, and that he has not the heart to take it out. {{lost}} great works are gone from {{city}}. The capital will hardly notice. The city notices every empty frame.

variants.headline: The {{wonder}} stands at {{city}}
body: {{city}} has completed the {{wonder}}. One of the people who worked on it brought her children to see what had kept her late; the youngest had never seen it without the boards the crews had put up around the site.

variants.headline: A wonder of our own is finished
body: The {{wonder}} is complete. The scaffolding is down, and the first people through the gate this morning stopped in the road to look. One of them has already come back with a neighbor.

variants.headline: Hear it, people of {{city}}! The {{wonder}} is done
body: The scaffolds are down! The {{wonder}} stands, finished and ours! Say it at the well, say it at the gate: it is ours, it is ours! Let the neighbors come and see what we build, and let them carry the sight home with them!

variants.headline: The innkeeper at {{city}}'s {{wonder}} orders a second cart
body: The innkeeper by the gate of {{city}} has ordered a second cart of ale for the yard. Travelers are already arriving to see it, and the masons who raised it are still in the city, their scaffolds stacked by the wall.

variants.headline: The children got there first
body: The last scaffold plank came down at noon, and by evening the children of {{city}} were playing beneath the {{wonder}}, every one of them promising to build a bigger one. The masons watched from the fence and did not chase them off.

variants.headline: The visitors come to {{civilization}} first
body: In {{civilization}}, a guide has added a second walk to her week, and the coach yard turns away carts by noon. The count now puts the country first at {{tourism}}, ahead of last season's leader.

variants.headline: A change at the top of the tourism table
body: First place in tourism has changed hands, with the new leader rated at {{tourism}}. A guide who keeps a folder of itineraries says customers have started asking what they might see if they took a different road this year.

variants.headline: The tourism lead goes to {{civilization}}
body: We are informed that the tourism table has a sole leader: {{civilization}}, with a rating of {{tourism}}. The editor of a travel almanac here says he will give the country the first pages of his next edition.

variants.headline: A share of first place for {{civilization}}
body: The visitors' count has {{civilization}} level with the best, at {{tourism}}. A booking clerk has stopped calling the choice obvious.

variants.headline: Tourism: No. 1 for {{civilization}}
body: {{tourism}} in the latest tourism table. That's enough for first place.
